project.name: PapaMap
project.description: Map of baby changing tables in 44 European countries plus Australia, New Zealand, the United States and Canada, coloured by whether a father can reach them.

tags.description: Selects every object the map shows. An explicit changing_table=no is kept, so a surveyed negative is not asked again.

Decides the colour of the pin. male_toilet, unisex_toilet, dedicated_room and outdoor are reachable by a father (green), female_toilet alone is not (red), and a missing value is the grey pin the map asks visitors to answer.
Shown in the popup for a place, falling back to fee when it is absent.
Counted for the coverage statistics (how many toilets carry a changing-table tag at all), and the layer the project's MapComplete theme lets people answer the question on.

A table behind a central key (RADAR in the UK) counts as unreachable only when the key locks the whole place or the cubicle the table is in — an open men's or women's section next to a locked accessible cubicle still counts.
Same rule as centralkey, for objects that record the restriction on access instead.
Badges a place as having somewhere for the child to play. An explicit kids_area:indoor=no overrules it.
The documented way to say the play area is indoors; settles the badge outright.
A commercial indoor playground, badged like kids_area.
Badged when combined with indoor=yes, which is the other way mappers record an indoor play area.
